# EEZ Quickstarts

> Fifteen interactive walkthroughs of the Ethereum Economic Zone, each built on real
> protocol source cited at a pinned commit rather than on pseudocode. Covers writing
> contracts that call across rollups, running the stack, and how Rollup0 settles and proves.

Every code panel on this site is rendered from JavaScript at runtime, so fetching a page
gives you the shell and not the content. These files hand over the content directly: each
walkthrough's narration and code, the full compilable Solidity behind the Solidity ones,
and the runnable Foundry tests.

Two things worth knowing before you use any of it. EEZ is pre-mainnet, so treat
capability claims as design intent rather than shipped behaviour; the proof system in the
public source is dev-grade ECDSA, not production ZK. And every citation here is pinned to
a commit SHA, so a link tells you exactly which revision a claim was true of.

## Dapp developers

Writing contracts that call across rollups.

- [How to get your contract's address on another rollup](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q7-your-cross-chain-address.html): Learn how to read it, deploy it, or let the protocol create it for you.
- [How do I call a contract on another rollup?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q2-send-a-cross-chain-call.html): Encode it like any normal call and send it to the proxy address. There is no cross-chain ABI to learn — the proxy's fallback catches everything and routes it. It even works out whether you meant a read: one self-call probes a transient write, and if that reverts, the call goes to a read-only lookup instead of a real execution.
- [Who is msg.sender when the call comes from another chain?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q3-fix-the-msg-sender-gotcha.html): The proxy — never your original address. A call from another rollup arrives through the proxy, so that is who the destination sees. A require(msg.sender == owner) written for same-chain use passes locally and reverts every time cross-chain. Whitelist the proxy instead.
- [How do I check an address is a real proxy?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q4-check-if-an-address-is-a-proxy.html): Read the registry — every proxy is recorded when it is created. One public mapping, no simulation and no guessing. When isProxy is true, the other two fields — the original address and its rollup id — are real.
- [What does the manager accept?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q6-why-you-cant-call-the-manager-directly.html): Calls that arrive through a registered proxy. Nothing else reaches execution. Call the manager's entry point directly and it reverts with UnauthorizedProxy(). Both proxy entry points open with that same check, so no call reaches execution without passing it.
- [How do I encode a call's content hash?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q5-encode-a-calls-content-hash.html): Eight fields, hashed in one fixed order, identify a cross-chain call. Hash them together and you get the bytes32 that identifies the call. The order is load-bearing: reorder the fields and the hash changes silently — no error, just a hash that nothing matches.

## Rollup operators

Standing the stack up and driving it.

- [How do I run the whole stack locally?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro1-run-the-devnet-with-kurtosis.html): Pull the submodule, start the engine, then one script boots the rest. A submodule pulls in the real contract source, kurtosis engine start spins up the disposable network, and two exports point it at the enclave and args file. Then one script deploys the contracts, generates the L2 genesis, and boots the L1, MEV-builder, node and proof-signer together — the same components you would run against a real testnet, without one.
- [How do I deploy the protocol?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro2-deploy-the-protocol.html): One command deploys the core protocol, the proof system and your manager. make deploy-protocol writes every address it produces into a gitignored deployments.env, and make run-node reads that file at startup — so there is no paste-the-address-into-.env step.
- [How do I run this against a real testnet?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro3-run-a-real-chiado-l2.html): The same stack, pointed at Chiado instead of a sandbox. One-time build tooling, then deploy-protocol writes deployments.env and genesis.json before docker compose starts the node, signer and lighthouse. cast block-number against both ports confirms the embedded L1 is climbing and the L2 is producing.
- [How do I send and test a cross-chain call?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro4-send-and-test-cross-chain-calls.html): Two proxy fronts, one script, real pass/fail numbers. Transparent fronts sit in front of L1 and L2: cross-chain transactions are held for the next sync block, everything else passes straight through. Watch EEZ_MAX_USER_TXS_PER_BUNDLE — it defaults to 3, and anything past it is dropped silently.

## Protocol researchers

How Rollup0 actually settles and proves.

- [Which component does what?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr1-the-four-components-of-rollup0.html): Four separate programs, not one node. The sequencer builds a chain's blocks; the composer settles any cross-chain calls inside them — the live path is just those two. The proof-signer then signs a hash of the result so the block can be trusted downstream. The deriver trusts none of them and re-derives the same state from L1 alone.
- [If L2 commits first, what makes L1 the source of truth?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr2-commit-first-repair-if-needed.html): L2 commits immediately, and L1 either settles it or repairs it. begin() commits the L2 block before L1 has confirmed anything, and that optimistic state waits at a fixed sync height until L1's history reaches it. L1 confirmation then marks it settled — or marks it failed and triggers a repair.
- [How does the composer prove a batch?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr4-how-the-composer-proves-a-batch.html): One gRPC stream: header first, then blocks, then a signature. The prover re-executes rather than taking the composer's word — it decodes the batch calldata, replays each block and recomputes the hash itself. The composer trusts the result only once the signature recovers to the registered attester.
- [Can the L2 chain be rebuilt from L1 alone?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr3-the-deriver.html): Yes — that is the deriver's entire job. It watches L1 for BatchPosted events rather than trusting any node's live output, rebuilding each slice of L2 state from raw L1 data. Replayed across all of L1 history, the resulting state answers to L1 and nothing else.
- [How is the address derived?](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr5-how-the-address-is-derived.html): Two values, hashed into a salt, run through CREATE2. The rollup id and your address, packed together, are the whole identity. keccak256 turns them into a 32-byte salt, and CREATE2 turns (manager, salt, bytecodeHash) into one address — computable before anything is deployed. This is the inside of computeCrossChainProxyAddress.

## Compilable source

Real files, not fragments: pragma, imports and a contract wrapper, all building under solc 0.8.28. Each mirrors the upstream function its walkthrough cites.

- [snippets/q7-create-proxy.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q7-create-proxy.sol): full source behind How to get your contract's address on another rollup
- [snippets/q2-cross-chain-call.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q2-cross-chain-call.sol): full source behind How do I call a contract on another rollup?
- [snippets/q3-msg-sender.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q3-msg-sender.sol): full source behind Who is msg.sender when the call comes from another chain?
- [snippets/q4-proxy-registry.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q4-proxy-registry.sol): full source behind How do I check an address is a real proxy?
- [snippets/q6-manager-direct.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q6-manager-direct.sol): full source behind What does the manager accept?
- [snippets/q5-content-hash.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q5-content-hash.sol): full source behind How do I encode a call's content hash?
- [snippets/q1-compute-address.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q1-compute-address.sol): full source behind How is the address derived?

## Runnable tests

Foundry tests with no forge-std and no submodules, so they drop into an existing suite. `cd snippets && forge test`.

- [snippets/test/Q3MsgSender.t.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/test/Q3MsgSender.t.sol): proves the behaviour in Who is msg.sender when the call comes from another chain?
- [snippets/test/Q6ManagerDirect.t.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/test/Q6ManagerDirect.t.sol): proves the behaviour in What does the manager accept?
- [snippets/test/Q5ContentHash.t.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/test/Q5ContentHash.t.sol): proves the behaviour in How do I encode a call's content hash?
